To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have cloned a cDNAs from Hydra that encodes a putative Notch-ligand, that is upregulated during budding and present in all cell layers of the adult Hydra, and that is localised in the cell membrane and in endosomal structures.
the Notch ligand is present in all celltypes of adult hydra and upregulated at a crucial step of budding.
HyJagged is expressed in all cell types and upregulated at bud-parent boundary, and is a potential ligand for Hvnotch.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, cloning and expression analysis of the putative Notch receptor HvNotch and of the Notch ligand, HyJagged, in the cnidarian Hydra.
the identification of the ligand for the Notch receptor in the Cnidarian model system Hydra.
the identification and characterisation of the endogenous Notch ligands and receptors in the Cnidarian hydra.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Notch signalling pathway in Hydra is not fully elucidated.
HyJagged is the ligand for HvN, however we cannot exclude that additional ligands exist.
the putative Notch Ligand HyJagged has a function in Hydra, which may include boundary formation during budding, as well as in adult hydra, possibly in the regulation of stem cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HyJagged is the first Notch ligand in Hydra and that it is a candidate for the formation of the boundary during budding.
HyJagged is expressed in all cells of adult hydra and localised to membranes and endocytic structures and that it is upregulated during budding in the bud-parent boundary.
HyJagged is an endogenous ligand of the HvNotch receptor, which may be involved in boundary formation during Hydra budding.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified the first Notch ligand in the basal Metazoa, which is conserved across all animal phyla.
the Notch pathway is highly conserved in Cindaria and is likely to be a key regulator in the formation of boundaries during development in this phylum.
we found a putative Notch-ligand in the cnidarian Hydra.
